options: How spread out the data is
The middle value of the data
questions.explanation: The range is the spread — largest minus smallest.
questions.misconception: Middle, frequent, and total describe the median, mode, and mean — the range is about the overall spread.
The range is a subtraction of extremes (45 − 8), not a single extreme, the middle, or the total.

questions.prompt: A small range means the data is...
questions.explanation: A small high-minus-low gap means the values sit close together.
questions.misconception: A small range shows closeness, not width — and values near a common level are bunched, not spread.

questions.prompt: Adding one very low value to a dataset makes the range...
questions.explanation: The new low stretches the high-minus-low gap, enlarging the range.
questions.misconception: An extreme at either end widens the distance, growing the range — not shrinking it.

questions.prompt: Two classes both have mean 70. What does their different range tell you?
options: How differently spread the scores are
questions.explanation: The range adds spread information the mean cannot show.
questions.misconception: Mean and range measure different things — the range says nothing about ability or correctness, only spread.
